7+ years of program or project management experience
Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements

Experience managing vendor and license agreements and purchasing/procurement coordination

Experience in regulatory compliance management with government agencies

jobs.title: Software Implementation Project Manager
jobs.description:
About 3E

3E is a mission-driven company dedicated to creating a safer and more sustainable world. We offer award-winning regulatory intelligence and AI solutions to help organizations protect people and products. With over 35 years of experience and a global presence, we empower our customers with innovative compliance solutions.

You will get to work at a company that combines startup agility with the stability of an industry leader. Partner with enterprise customers and global experts to advance environmental safety and solve complex data science challenges.

Join us and make an impact!

About The Role

As an Implementation Project Manager at 3E, you’ll lead larger, more complex customer implementations where successful delivery requires multiple products, technical contributors, workstreams, dependencies, and stakeholders to operate against one coordinated plan.

You’ll be accountable for turning the customer’s scope of work into an executable implementation strategy and for determining whether the overall project succeeds—on time, within scope, adopted, and connected to a clear customer outcome. You’ll establish success and acceptance criteria, own the integrated project plan, manage risk and change, coordinate specialists and technical teams, and give both customers and 3E leadership a clear, data-backed view of project health.

You’ll understand the technical delivery deeply enough to challenge assumptions, identify dependencies, connect customer needs with the right specialists, and engage credibly with Product and Engineering. You won’t need to personally execute every configuration, migration, or integration; your role is to ensure those pieces come together into a successful customer outcome.

This position supports remote work within the Eastern time zone.

What You’ll Do

Lead complex new-logo, cross-sell, and Value Realization implementations from internal handoff through customer acceptance and formal close.
Translate complex scopes of work into an integrated delivery strategy covering products, workstreams, milestones, resources, dependencies, assumptions, exclusions, and acceptance criteria.
Lead technical discovery and pre-integration planning with customers, CX technical specialists, and relevant internal teams.
Own the master implementation plan and coordinate implementation specialists, Product, Engineering, Data, Cloud, technical consultants, external partners, and customer resources.
Establish measurable success and acceptance criteria at kickoff and maintain accountability for those outcomes throughout delivery.
Lead customer project governance, including senior stakeholder and sponsor communications.
Maintain the milestone tracker and conduct phase-gate reviews, giving a clear assessment of whether projects are on track, at risk, or behind and establishing mitigation plans when required.
Identify cross-workstream dependencies and risks early and determine their impact on the critical path.
Lead complex, multi-product delivery by managing scope and change control, coordinating custom development through launch, maintaining a unified customer plan across teams, and providing leadership with clear, data-backed reporting on project health, risk, timelines, value, and adoption.
Build and maintain dashboards or reporting tools that make project status and risks visible without relying solely on status meetings.
Lead customer escalations diplomatically while maintaining accountability for customer commitments, decisions, resources, data readiness, and signoffs.
Partner with Commercial on implementation handoff and identify expansion opportunities or renewal risks surfaced during delivery.
Represent the delivery perspective during pre-sales scoping of complex or higher-risk opportunities so commitments can be successfully delivered.
Drive structured post-onboarding Value Realization Projects, including complex migrations, integrations, optimization, remediation, and workflow initiatives.
Manage multiple concurrent implementations and make prioritization decisions based on risk, complexity, dependencies, and customer impact.
Identify opportunities to improve implementation processes, delivery predictability, time-to-value, and the overall customer experience.

Required

What Makes You a Great Fit

3–5 years of experience in software implementation, customer onboarding, technical account or project management, or professional services, ideally within B2B SaaS, technology, or information services.
Demonstrated experience leading complex customer implementations with multiple workstreams, technical dependencies, contributors, or products.
Experience owning project scope, plans, milestones, risks, dependencies, change control, customer communication, and delivery outcomes.
Strong technical aptitude and the ability to understand configuration, data, integration, and technical delivery sufficiently to coordinate specialists and identify risk; coding is not required.
Demonstrated ability to lead customer conversations and communicate credibly with senior customer stakeholders.
Ability to lead and influence cross-functional contributors without formal authority.
Experience managing multiple concurrent projects and making informed prioritization decisions based on customer and business impact.
Strong written and verbal communication, analytical thinking, judgment, and problem-solving skills.
Proficiency with CRM tools such as Salesforce or HubSpot and Microsoft Office, with comfort using data, dashboards, and systems of record to communicate project health.
Ability to navigate ambiguity and changing scope while maintaining accountability for outcomes.
Willingness to travel 10–20%.

Preferred

Bachelor’s degree in business, information systems, environmental science, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Experience with enterprise and/or mid-market SaaS customers.
Experience developing or improving implementation processes and customer journeys.
Familiarity with implementation, onboarding, or enablement tools such as Pendo, Gong, or Zendesk.
Experience working with time-to-value, adoption, usage, or customer health metrics.
Exposure to environmental, regulatory, compliance, chemical management, SDS, EHS, or sustainability software.
Multilingual capability and/or experience supporting global customers.

This role must be based in one of the states where 3E is authorized to hire, and eligible to work without sponsorship.

Our US Benefits Include

Health, dental, and vision insurance
Life insurance and disability coverage
Open PTO and parental leave
401(k) plan with company matching
Employee assistance program
Voluntary supplemental benefits (Accident, Hospital Indemnity, Critical Illness)

Alabama, Arizona, California (excluding Los Angeles), Colorado (excluding Denver), Connecticut, Delaware, District of Columbia, Florida, Georgia, Illinois (excluding Chicago), Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New York (excluding New York City), North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Virginia, and Washington.

Description

Leidos Security Operations is seeking an experienced and mission-driven Executive Protection Program Manager to lead protective operations for our executive leadership team within a high-security, high-compliance defense industry environment. This role will ensure the safety, security, and operational continuity of executives during domestic and international travel, corporate events, and site visits.

The Executive Protection Manager will work closely with threat intelligence, corporate security, cybersecurity, and compliance teams to ensure that protective measures meet operational needs.

The job is based at Leidos Global Headquarters in Reston, Virginia.

Primary Responsibilities

Reporting to the Chief Security Officer, the selectee will be responsible for:

Lead and manage executive protection operations for the CEO, executive leadership team, and Board of Director members in alignment with corporate security protocols and U.S. government regulations.
Recruiting, training, and leading a three-person team comprised of two protection professionals and one executive driver ensuring training, readiness, and operational discipline.
Conduct threat, vulnerability, and risk assessments for all executive-attended events, movements, external meetings, and site visits to ensure their safety.
Engaging and collaborating cross-functionally on event and travel schedules and planning to ensure robust protection of key stakeholders.
Coordinate closely with security analysts, Global Resilience security, and government security agencies to ensure accurate situational awareness.
Coordinating, budgeting, and managing contracted external services and assessments in support of the Executive Protection Program.
Planning, and executing the Program’s operational budget.
Assessing, documenting, implementing and enforcing use of force practices, armed protection requirements, and training curriculum as well as proposing changes to policies, procedures, and playbooks related to the Program.
Integrate cybersecurity and physical security considerations into all executive protection planning.
Ensuring all protection operations comply with company policies and legal requirements while maintaining the highest standards of professionalism and discretion.
Provide executive leadership with discreet situational intelligence briefings on relevant geopolitical, terrorism, and criminal threats.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelors degree and 8+ years of executive protection, preferably with corporate security experience, with 3+ years in a leadership or management role. Additional years experience may be used in lieu of a degree.
Experience supporting executives or high-value assets in sensitive environments.
Completion of a recognized executive protection training course
Strong working knowledge of threat assessment, advance planning, emergency medical response, and protective operations in compliance-heavy industries.
Proven ability to coordinate with U.S. government security agencies (DSS, FBI, DHS, etc.) and understand relevant security clearance protocols.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to brief senior executives and collaborate at all levels.
Current CPR and AED medical certifications.
Valid driver’s license with clean driving record; defensive/evasive driving training.
Willingness to travel (including OCONUS) and work some non-standard hours based on executive requirements.
Must meet all Virginia Department of Criminal Justice Services Personal Protection Specialist requirements with the ability to successfully achieve certifications in armed and unarmed personal protection specialist as well as basic and advanced handgun
Proven ability to maintain composure in dealing with authorities, executives, clients, staff, and the public, including under conditions of urgency and in high-pressure situations
Must be physically fit to provide protective coverage during physically taxing activities
Knowledge of unarmed self-defense tactics (use of force)
Must be a US citizen with ability to obtain a Top Secret security clearance
Possess superior critical thinking skills, analytic ability, creativity, keen attention to detail, and problem-solving skills to address unanticipated issues
Proven ability as a self-starter who can work independently and as part of a team to deliver high value customer support

Preferred Qualifications

Current Top Secret security clearance
Bachelor’s degree in Security Management, Criminal Justice, or related field
Experience at the senior organizational level leading dynamic teams
Experience integrating protective intelligence, cyber threat data, and physical security operations
Active Paramedic, First Responder, and Emergency Medical Technician certifications
Experience operating security camera systems/CCTV, access control, and alarm systems
Experience responding to workplace violence issues
De-escalation training
Possess a valid Virginia concealed handgun permit or be eligible to carry under the Law Enforcement Officer Safety Act or HR218
Technical Surveillance Counter Measures experience
Open-source intelligence training or experience

Delivering essential infrastructure services for life, while being safety first and client and customer centric in a friendly, fun and respectful environment where you are encouraged to thrive.

Where will you be working?

We help our clients safeguard the water supply, improve environmental performance and manage demand for future generations. We enhance and extend asset life, ensuring compliance with water quality and environmental standards. We’re problem solvers with over 140 years of combined experience in engineering and infrastructure.

This role will be within our water and wastewater capital project delivery team. Our teams deliver large-scale capital programmes aimed at keeping water infrastructure resilient for the long-term while protecting the environment.

Want to be a part of it?

What will you be doing?

You'll have the opportunity to mentor and lead project teams, fostering a collaborative and productive work environment

You'll develop an environment where staff share ideas and best practice. Problem solve, identify risks and develop mitigation strategies. Ensuring projects are delivered in a safe, efficient, timely way and promoting best practice in quality management.

We'll need you to deliver excellent customer service and achieve above target customer satisfaction scores. Minimise/reduce the number of complaints received. Increase productivity, without compromising on safety and continuously drive efficiency.

Who We Are

We are Tennis! The USTA (United States Tennis Association) is the national governing body for the sport of tennis and the leader in promoting and developing the sport’s growth on every level in the United States, from local communities to the crown jewel of the professional game, the US Open.

The USTA Foundation Incorporated (USTAF or USTA Foundation) is the social impact arm of the United States Tennis Association Incorporated (USTA), utilizing the powerful combination of tennis and education to enhance the lives of under-resourced youth through its support of the National Junior Tennis & Learning (NJTL) network. For more than 50 years, NJTL has impacted thousands of under-resourced youth across the nation, and today the network features more than 270 chapters that reach more than 233,000,000 young people from under-resourced communities annually.

Why Work for the USTA?

We are a passionate team of staff and volunteers focused on growing the sport of tennis and making it accessible to all. We are committed to removing barriers and creating opportunities for ALL to participate.

About Lulu's Place

Lulu's Place will offer state-of-the-art facilities in Los Angeles, north of LAX airport, between the communities of Westchester and Playa del Rey, bringing together academic, athletic, and wellness programs for youth from all backgrounds. Trusted partners, including TGR Foundation, a Tiger Woods charity; the United States Tennis Association (USTA) and its charitable arm, USTA Foundation; Cedars-Sinai; and Providence will bring together professional teachers, coaches, mentors, and service providers to deliver high-quality programs to children and their families.

The vision for this project is rooted in the passion and generosity of Carol "Lulu" Kimmelman, a Southern California native, former elementary school teacher in South Los Angeles, and lifelong tennis player who passed away in 2017 after a courageous battle with ovarian cancer. Today, her husband, Doug Kimmelman, and their four children honor Lulu's legacy by advancing her mission to transform young people's lives and create greater equity in sports and education through this groundbreaking youth center.

The Role

The Program Manager will support the youth development program focused on college and career readiness and non-degree career pathways, working within a shared facility alongside several partner organizations. This role is responsible for day-to-day program execution and direct oversight of program staff. Includes partner integration and collaboration on programmatic delivery.

Day-to-Day Program Execution

Operational Oversight: Manage day-to-day operations for USTAF Center for Innovation programming, ensuring all activities align with the foundation’s mission, goals, priorities, and safety standards.
Partner and Site Integration: Coordinate with the program staff of Lulu's Place, TGR Foundation, and other on-site program partners to execute educational and tennis programming and achieve shared goals.
Coordinate day-to-day use of shared space, equipment, and resources with co-located partner organizations
Serve as the on-site liaison for partner organizations on operational and scheduling matters (e.g., room bookings, shared equipment, daily logistics)
Escalate any partner matters involving cost, liability, space allocation disputes, or agreement terms to the Executive Director rather than resolving them directly

Community Engagement: Works closely with the USTAF Lulu's Place Operations Director/Manager to ensure that the local community partners, including local NJTL organizations, school districts, youth development organizations, and other key community stakeholders, are incorporated into daily and weekly programming
Quality Assurance: Responsible for the oversight and delivery of USTAF programs and partnered programs to accomplish established and shared goals.
Ensure program sessions, workshops, and events run on time and as planned, including opening/closing logistics.
Ensure program spaces are set up, maintained, and left in appropriate condition after use.
Troubleshoot and resolve day-to-day operational issues (scheduling conflicts, space usage, materials, technology, attendance) as they arise

Record Keeping: Maintain daily and weekly program logs, attendance records, and activity documentation
Collect and maintain accurate data on student enrollment, attendance, participation, and outcomes for core programming, following data definitions and quality standards set by the Executive Director and Lulu's Place leadership.
Prepare regular reports on program activities and metrics for the Program Director and Lulu's Place Leadership
Support grant reporting by compiling relevant program data and documentation
Maintain organized records and files related to program operations

Asset Inventory: Monitor and maintain inventory of program materials and supplies, placing orders or requests as needed
Safety: Ensure day-to-day compliance with youth safety policies, including check-in/check-out procedures and supervision ratios
Compliance: Support the Program Director in implementing organizational policies and procedures at the staff level
Strategic direction: Identify opportunities to test and expand programs/products to increase the reach and enhance the impact of NJTL sports-based interventions within the community.

Staff Supervision & Support

Directly supervise a team of full-time and part-time program staff, mentors, and coordinators for core high school and middle school programming
Provide administrative supervision of the Outreach Coordinator (scheduling, timesheets, day-to-day check-ins); the Outreach Coordinator's programmatic priorities and calendar are set jointly by the Executive Director and Outreach Coordinator and should be respected as protected, not reassigned to cover core programming needs
Create and manage staff schedules, ensuring adequate coverage across all program activities and age groups
Provide day-to-day coaching, guidance, and support to staff on curriculum delivery and student engagement
Conduct regular check-ins and team meetings with program staff
Onboard and train new staff and volunteers on program procedures, policies, and expectations
Monitor staff performance and provide feedback; escalate performance concerns to the Program Director, who holds final hiring and termination authority
Approve staff timesheets and time-off requests in accordance with organizational policy

Curriculum & Activity Coordination

Coordinate the delivery of college and career readiness curriculum, workshops, and mentorship sessions for high school and middle school students
Coordinate with the Outreach Coordinator to align core programming with elementary/middle school outreach efforts where relevant, without absorbing outreach staffing or scheduling into core program operations
Work with staff to adapt lesson plans and activities to meet the needs of different age groups and skill levels
Coordinate guest speakers, site visits, employer partners, and other enrichment activities
Track and ensure completion of program milestones and deliverables tied to funder or grant requirements

Student & Family Communication

Serve as the primary daily point of contact for student and family questions, concerns, and updates related to core programming
Communicate regularly with parents/guardians regarding schedules, events, and student progress
Monitor student participation and follow up on attendance issues or disengagement
Address day-to-day behavioral or logistical issues, escalating more serious concerns to the Program Director

Who You Are

Education: A bachelor’s degree in a related field such as Sports Management, Recreation Administration, Education, Social Work, or Non-Profit Management is required.
Work Experience: 3 to 5 years of experience in program coordination, youth development, or sports administration. Tennis background and/or understanding of the tennis environment is required.
Partner Management: Proven track record of managing relationships with community partners, schools, or diverse local organizations is required.
Safety Certifications: Valid CPR, First Aid, and AED certifications (or the ability to obtain them within 30 days of hire) are required.
Clearance: Ability to pass comprehensive, recurring federal and state background checks to work with minors is required.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (especially Excel) and Google Workspace is required. Experience using CRMs or program management software is preferred.
Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation for travel between facility sites is required.
Schedule Flexibility: Ability to work non-traditional hours, including evenings and weekends, to align with youth sports schedules is required.
Physical Stamina: Ability to be mobile and active on sports courts or fields for extended periods and lift/move equipment up to 50 lbs is required.

What We Offer

At the USTA, we know people are our most important asset. For this reason, we offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to meet the needs of a diverse workforce!

Flexibility: Our Hybrid with Flexibility approach combines a balance of remote working with in-office collaboration to spark teamwork and creativity.
Comprehensive benefits designed to meet your unique needs: Medical, dental, vision, access to doctors virtually, a flexible spending account to manage your health and dependent care expenses, and life and disability insurance are a small part of our offerings.
Time to recharge and energize: Generous paid time off policy - including vacation, sick, personal, and paid holidays, parental leave, and a paid winter recess.
Plan for your future financially and professionally: 401(k) with employer matching (up to 6.5%), promotional and growth opportunities, Learning and Development programs to learn on the job, and up to $7,000 for tuition reimbursement.
Mental and emotional wellness: Resources for overall well-being, including mental health and meditation benefits.
Other cool perks: A personalized health management program, pet insurance, commuter benefits, identity theft protection, discounts with our network of partners, and fun events are just a few of the optional benefits available.

The expected range for the annual base salary for this position is $75,000 - 90,000.
This role is eligible for an Incentive Compensation Plan (ICP) bonus up to 5%. This range does not include any additional pay or benefits for which a person may qualify. The actual base salary offered is determined by several variables, including, as appropriate, the applicant's qualifications for the position, the years of relevant experience, their unique skills, and the location from which they will be performing the job.

Hybrid: Los Angeles

The Legal Project Manager collaborates with attorneys, administrative professionals, and clients to manage the status, resources, and timelines for a variety of projects, and works with colleagues to provide updates on issues to ensure deadlines are communicated and met, and provides oversight of trademark and copyright research and projects.

This is a hybrid position that requires in-office attendance at our Los Angeles office two days per week. On days when in-person attendance is not required, the individual may work remotely, subject to approval by their direct supervisor (and assigned attorneys, if applicable). · Create long and short-term plans, including tracking progress of phases and tasks, setting targets for milestones and adhering to deadlines.

·Make effective decisions when presented with multiple options for how to progress a project.
·Serve as a point of contact when multiple colleagues are assigned to the same project to ensure team actions remain in synergy.

· Adjust schedules and targets on projects as needed or as project scope changes.

· Manage the administrative functions, such as the preparation and formatting of written communications, reporting, or presentations, client intake, and billing; maintain and update client files and communication as directed.
· Ensure proper technology is leveraged to execute both project-coordination and financial-tracking tasks.
· Set the calendar and own the daily itinerary as well as any meeting deliverables, communications, or follow-up.
· Oversight of client status reports, research projects, and client communications related to the supported practice area.

Required Skills, Abilities and Qualifications:

· Must be a proactive, self-starter who is detail-oriented and can integrate particulars into a larger, strategic context.
·Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to explain financial and budget information clearly to attorneys and clients.
· Excellent organizational skills and a high level of attention to detail.
·Experience with researching, collecting, analyzing, and reporting on data, including matter financial data.
·Customer service orientation, commitment to meeting deadlines, and ability to multitask in a fast-paced and dynamic environment.
·Strong, independent problem-solving and the ability to offer constructive opinions and creative solutions.
·A team player who motivates and educates other team members.
·Must have flexibility to work outside scheduled hours as required.
·Exceptional technology skills, with expert-level knowledge of Outlook, Smartsheet, and other project management platforms.

·Minimum of 3-5 years of experience in a law firm environment, including exposure to matter budgeting, billing, alternative fee arrangements, or financial reporting.

All Hanson Bridgett employees are expected to demonstrate excellence in how we serve our clients and support our colleagues, upholding the firm’s values as part of our culture. Specific expectations include:

·Communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, with clients, attorneys, business professionals, and external audiences.

·Meet deadlines, manage competing priorities, and commit to meeting high standards.

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Syteline Business Analyst to lead functional design, configuration, testing and deployment of Syteline (Infor CloudSuite Industrial) ERP solutions. The role partners with business stakeholders and technical teams to gather requirements, perform gap analysis, define solutions, manage integrations and support go-live and post-implementation activities to ensure the ERP delivers expected business value.

Collaborate with stakeholders to elicit and document business requirements, use cases, user stories and functional specifications for Syteline implementations and enhancements.
Perform business process analysis, gap analysis and solution design across Procure-to-Pay, Order-to-Cash, Inventory, MRP/Manufacturing, Fixed Assets, HCM/Payroll and Financial modules (GL/AP/AR).
Configure and validate Syteline system settings and support safe customization where needed, ensuring alignment with best practices and governance.
Design, execute and oversee integration and data migration activities including data mapping, ETL processes, EDI, REST/SOAP APIs and middleware coordination.
Develop and execute test plans, test cases and UAT scripts; coordinate integration testing, UAT and defect resolution with technical teams and business users.
Create and maintain implementation artifacts including BRDs, functional specifications, process diagrams (Visio/Lucidchart), training materials and release documentation.
Partner with technical teams on reporting and analytics requirements, supporting SQL/PL/SQL, T-SQL, SSRS, Power BI, Tableau or Crystal Reports delivery where applicable.
Work within Agile (Scrum) and Waterfall project methodologies, using tools such as JIRA, Confluence, HP ALM or TestRail to manage requirements, sprints and defects.

jobs.title: Insider Threat Program Analyst
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

INSIDER THREAT PROGRAM ANALYST

SpaceX is seeking a dynamic and driven individual with a demonstrated ability to work independently and as a member of a team in a fast-paced, high-tech environment. Our goal is to protect some of the world’s most advanced technologies including rockets, Dragon capsules for human transport, inter-planetary transport vehicles, the world's largest satellite communications network, etc. As an industry leader, we are a target of adversaries, both foreign and domestic, focused on slowing us down and accessing our proprietary technology. The work we do will literally safeguard mankind becoming an interplanetary species.

You will be responsible for the research, analysis, production, and dissemination of information relevant to protecting the safety and security of personnel, brand, global assets, intellectual property, and operations at SpaceX. This role will triage anomalous event data and analyze insider threat program datasets to respond to threats posed to SpaceX. You will use comprehensive understanding of various collection methods and platforms to explore new data sources, build effective queries, and combine information from disparate sources.

Responsibilities

Conduct comprehensive investigations and analysis in support of SpaceX intellectual property and security
Uphold investigation and analytic tradecraft standards including confidentiality, objectivity, lawfulness, timeliness, and use of all available sources of information
Collect and analyze available program data to evaluate insider threat risk to SpaceX infrastructure, programs, and operations
Triage anomalous event data associated with indicators of data exfiltration, data destruction and other key indicators of concern
Conduct internal investigations working with Information Security, HR, Legal, Government Security, Physical Security, and external partners based on information derived from internal and external sources
Utilize network monitoring, data analytic, and other tools (DLP/SIEM/UEBA) to identify anomalous activity, initiate investigations and decipher underlying trends
Extract and organize insider threat program data to build metrics, reports and case studies addressing mission requirements and timelines
Communicate findings in a timely and accurate manner to team members, management, and relevant stakeholders
Support employee training and briefings for internal and external audiences
Liaise with external industry and government partners to benchmark insider threat program, share threat intelligence, and further investigations
Continuously identify and help implement program improvement methods
Manage and safeguard sensitive information, including case files, employee PII, and intelligence reports

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree and 2+ years of professional experience in internal investigations, information security, or counterintelligence; OR 4+ years professional experience in information security, internal investigations, or counterintelligence in lieu of a degree

Preferred Skills And Experience

1+ year using a SIEM and/or conducting digital forensic investigations in a government or corporate environment
Working level understanding of insider threat program missions, internal stakeholders, and manifestations of insider threats
Proficiency in Microsoft Purview for eDiscovery
Experience performing business process automation or constructing data pipelines
Familiarity with risk-based alerting, detection, and tuning concepts for insider risk
Experience conducting preliminary assessments, determining scope, investigation planning, evidence collection/handling, interviewing and reporting findings to internal and external stakeholders
Ability to conduct interviews on short notice according to established internal guidelines.
Excellent written and oral communication skills, with the ability to produce clear and concise reports
Highly organized with a strong attention to detail
Ability to adapt to changing priorities and deadlines
Can swiftly adapt to new technical environments and workflows
Ability to exercise discretion when conducting confidential investigations

Additional Requirements

Must be able to work extended hours and weekends as needed to support critical efforts and operations
Must be willing to travel ad hoc
Active TS/SCI clearance, or ability to obtain one. With an active clearance, candidates will be subject to pre-employment screening including background check and drug/alcohol test as well as random drug and alcohol testing during employment

Compensation And Benefits

Pay Range:

Level 1: $85,000 - $110,000

Level 2: $100,000 - $135,000

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

Those with an active clearance will receive a 10% differential, up to an additional $20,000 annually, once officially briefed into a classified program.

Itar Requirements

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C.
1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C.
1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

Red Bull North America’s Commercial Data team ensures distributor trade sales data is accurate, complete, and reliable across RBNA systems. Sitting within Trade Finance, the Commercial Data Team partners with business stakeholders, distributors, and technical teams to create a trusted data foundation for reporting and decision-making. As subject-matter experts, team members collaborate to establish consistent data standards, promote proper data structure and usage, and help stakeholders use commercial data effectively.

The Commercial Data team is hiring a Data Analyst to support business reporting and drives continuous improvements in data ingestion, processing, and governance. Reporting to the Manager, Commercial Data, the Data Analyst monitors data received from distributor RAS and ERP systems, investigates reporting discrepancies, and partners with internal teams, distributors, and third-party vendors to resolve data issues. Success requires strong analytical and communication skills, close attention to detail, and the ability to translate business needs into clear technical requirements.

All the responsibilities we'll trust you with:

DATA QUALITY AND SYSTEMS INTEGRATION

Partner with the third-party data processing vendor to ensure high-quality distributor data flows into Red Bull systems and is available for company use. Partner with distributor technical contacts to investigate and resolve data issues, communicate business impacts to internal stakeholders, and escalate unresolved issues as needed. Gather project requirements from sales teams and guide communication between business and IT partners to translate business needs into clear technical requirements. Collaborate with internal and third-party teams on ongoing data quality projects and system enhancements.

COMMERCIAL DATA ANALYSIS AND REPORTING

Develop proficiency in the SAP BI reporting interface and Red Bull trade sales data structure. Support Red Bull users in creating accurate reports for business needs. Perform ad hoc data analysis and provide hands-on support for complex reporting challenges. Compare internal and external data sources to identify, investigate, and resolve reporting discrepancies.

PROCESS IMPROVEMENT

Support the Commercial Data team with process documentation and system enhancements related to data ingestion, processing, and structural organization. Recommend process improvements that strengthen data quality and operational efficiency. Apply technical skills to modernize reporting and data monitoring capabilities.

Your areas of knowledge and expertise that matter most for this role:

1+ years of relevant professional experience.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including comparing datasets and managing large spreadsheets.
Familiarity with data management practices, business systems, and reporting tools.
Working knowledge of database structures and basic querying; SQL experience is preferred.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate business needs into technical requirements.
CPG industry experience is preferred but not required.

This position is open to U.S. citizens, U.S. permanent residents, or individuals who are currently authorized to work in the United States on a valid visa.

The base salary range for this position is $72,000 - $108,000 + cash incentives. Actual salary offers may vary based on work experience. The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified.

Our current Benefits include:

Comprehensive Medical, Dental and Vision Plans, 401k Match, Family Leave, PTO & Paid Holiday Schedule, Pet, Legal, and Life Insurance, Tuition Reimbursement (Benefits listed may vary depending on the nature of your employment and/or work location)

ESA Headquarters, Paris, France

Description

ASTRIS Project Manager, Ariane Programme, Directorate of Space Transportation

Under the authority of the Head of the Ariane Programme, you will be responsible for the technical and programmatic implementation of the ASTRIS development and the preparation of its exploitation, managing all relevant resources and contracts. As such, you will be responsible for the Astris funds, georeturn, risks, margins and schedules in cooperation with the Business Unit Control Office.

Your tasks and responsibilities will include:

managing the technical and programmatic implementation of the ASTRIS development, composed of a space segment and a ground control segment, including specifications elaboration, design, development, qualification assembly of the first article;
preparing the exploitation organization with the various stakeholder and contributing to the preparation of the first missions;
preparing the relevant Statement of works, request for quotation, evaluation of industrial offers and conducting negotiations related to procurement in your area of responsibility;
interfacing with industry for the implementation of the project’s activities, managing the industrial contract(s);
managing the team in charge of Astris and the associated support from the Directorate of Technology, Engineering and Quality (TEC) and the possible integrated support provided by national organisations;
preparing the relevant project plans and organizing the integrated project reviews;
managing the overall budget allocated to the programme;
reporting of the status and criticalities of the activities in your domain of responsibility on a weekly basis with line management;
preparing the relevant document for the reporting and interfacing with concerned delegations and to the programme board.

You will be assisted by a project team under your direct responsibility, and will receive engineering, PA, safety, procurement and project control support from the Ariane 6 program teams and associated support functions.

Knowledge of project management techniques

Background in the design, development, assembly, integration, testing and acceptance of systems for space applications

Result Orientation

Operational Efficiency

Fostering Cooperation

Relationship Management

Continuous Improvement

Forward Thinking

Direct experience in the development of space programmes
Proven experience of leading, motivating and developing a team in a project environment
The ability to provide strategic direction to the individuals and teams within the Astris project and to relate team objectives to the overall, evolving organisational goals and context
The ability to drive performance and foster cooperation within and across teams throughout the organisation
Demonstrated excellent leadership, relationship management and communication skills, both oral and written
A proven track record of representing the Agency’s interests to external interfaces
Excellent cognitive, analytical, delegation, planning and organisational skills
The ability to anticipate problems, solve complex issues and relate situations to their context
The ability to reach solution-oriented, pragmatic and timely decisions of a high standard and with integrity as well as to support others (team members, upper management, other stakeholders) in this process

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
jobs.description:
Terra AI is building a new category at the intersection of artificial intelligence, geoscience, and critical resource development.

As global demand for copper, lithium, nickel, rare earth elements, geothermal energy, and other strategic resources accelerates, the mining and subsurface industries face a growing challenge: traditional exploration methods remain slow, expensive, and highly uncertain. Terra AI was founded to help solve this problem by redefining how critical resources are discovered, evaluated, and developed.

By combining advanced machine learning, probabilistic modeling, and deep geoscience expertise, Terra AI helps exploration and mining companies make faster, more informed subsurface decisions with greater confidence and capital efficiency. The company’s platform integrates geological, geophysical, and drilling data into intelligent systems designed to improve targeting accuracy, accelerate discovery timelines, and reduce exploration risk.

Backed by Khosla Ventures, BHP, and Rio Tinto, Terra AI works with industry leaders to bring a more informed, data-driven approach to critical resource development.

Terra AI’s mission is to define the new global standard for data-driven critical resource development — breaking the cost and time curve required to support electrification, energy security, and the global energy transition.

The company operates with a strong partnership mentality, combining technical rigor, candid communication, continual learning, and environmental stewardship to help modern exploration teams solve some of the world’s most important resource challenges.

Who you are

You’re a seasoned project manager who’s comfortable learning as you go. Experience has taught you what good looks like, where projects tend to break down, and when a little structure can prevent a lot of pain later.

Technical complexity doesn’t intimidate you. You’ve worked closely with scientists and engineers and can absorb complicated information deeply enough to ask good questions, connect the dots, and help teams make sound decisions. You know when a project needs flexibility and room to move—and when it’s time to bring in more structure, process, or discipline.

You are calm under pressure, and in front of high-value customers. You communicate clearly, exercise good judgment, own mistakes when they happen, and help create an environment where others can do the same.

Strong written and visual communication is part of the craft. You can write a paragraph at least as good as this one without the help of an LLM, and you have the editorial judgment to know when a document or slide deck is genuinely ready to present—or when it still needs another pass.

What You’ll Do

This role sits at the center of our customer engagements, bringing together teams of geoscientists, software engineers, and AI/ML engineers to solve complex problems in projects that run for a few months at a time. The work is highly collaborative and varied—from early assessment and scoping through data review and processing, development of code and configurations, machine learning, and ultimately validating and tuning the results.

You will establish yourself as a trusted presence with our customers. Our projects involve high-value relationships around the world, with conversations happening both in person and remotely across time zones. Clear communication matters here, whether that means translating complex technical work for a broader audience, helping a teammate sharpen a presentation, or making sure everyone leaves a conversation with the same understanding of what comes next.

Keeping our projects moving takes equal parts organization, judgment, and curiosity. There are schedules and checklists to manage, decisions to make, changes to navigate, and moments when leadership needs to weigh in. But some of the most important contributions are less procedural: asking the question that helps a team see a problem differently, creating space for a better idea to emerge, helping people through an obstacle, and making sure great work gets recognized when the team succeeds.

We’ve built tools and processes to support this work, but we don’t consider any of them finished. There’s plenty of room to improve what exists, challenge how we do things today, and help build what comes next.

Core Responsibilities

Serve as a primary point of contact across multiple overlapping client projects, owning day-to-day project management and helping ensure successful delivery
Set and manage clear expectations with customers and internal teams throughout each engagement
Build and maintain project plans covering scope, timelines, milestones, risks, decisions, and completion status
Keep important information, decisions, and action items, from falling through the cracks, and make sure commitments are met
Track project health and prioritize using both metrics and your expert judgment
Help improve the playbooks, tools, and templates that allow us to run more client engagements in parallel without sacrificing quality
Identify and manage risks and issues: bring the right people together to resolve them, and escalate thoughtfully when needed
Plan and facilitate effective internal and customer meetings, with clear agendas, decisions, and next steps
Create clear, polished customer-facing materials and help technical team members communicate their work effectively

Qualifications

10+ years of experience in project management, technical program management, implementation, professional services, or a similar role
Experience in a rapidly scaling startup environment is a strong plus
Experience working directly with enterprise customers, ideally delivering software products or services to demanding clients
Demonstrated ability to work closely with scientists and engineers, understanding enough underlying technology to ask good questions and drive great decisions
Experience with software, AI/ML, earth science, physics, or statistical analysis is a plus, but we don’t expect expertise across all of them
Strong judgment around when to introduce structure and process, and when flexibility is the better answer
A solutions-oriented mindset and a track record of navigating ambiguity, changing priorities, and complex projects
Excellent written, verbal, and visual communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across both technical and non-technical audiences
Multilingual communication skills (strong English required, Spanish is a strong plus)
Hybrid work environment at our Redwood City headquarters is preferred; we will consider a remote first role for well qualified candidates residing in the United States, Canada, or Mexico.
All candidates must be legally authorized to live and work, without visa sponsorship, in The United States, Canada, or Mexico.

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
jobs.description:
Terra AI is building a new category at the intersection of artificial intelligence, geoscience, and critical resource development.

As global demand for copper, lithium, nickel, rare earth elements, geothermal energy, and other strategic resources accelerates, the mining and subsurface industries face a growing challenge: traditional exploration methods remain slow, expensive, and highly uncertain. Terra AI was founded to help solve this problem by redefining how critical resources are discovered, evaluated, and developed.

By combining advanced machine learning, probabilistic modeling, and deep geoscience expertise, Terra AI helps exploration and mining companies make faster, more informed subsurface decisions with greater confidence and capital efficiency. The company’s platform integrates geological, geophysical, and drilling data into intelligent systems designed to improve targeting accuracy, accelerate discovery timelines, and reduce exploration risk.

Backed by Khosla Ventures, BHP, and Rio Tinto, Terra AI works with industry leaders to bring a more informed, data-driven approach to critical resource development.

Terra AI’s mission is to define the new global standard for data-driven critical resource development — breaking the cost and time curve required to support electrification, energy security, and the global energy transition.

The company operates with a strong partnership mentality, combining technical rigor, candid communication, continual learning, and environmental stewardship to help modern exploration teams solve some of the world’s most important resource challenges.

Who you are

You’re a seasoned project manager who’s comfortable learning as you go. Experience has taught you what good looks like, where projects tend to break down, and when a little structure can prevent a lot of pain later.

Technical complexity doesn’t intimidate you. You’ve worked closely with scientists and engineers and can absorb complicated information deeply enough to ask good questions, connect the dots, and help teams make sound decisions. You know when a project needs flexibility and room to move—and when it’s time to bring in more structure, process, or discipline.

You are calm under pressure, and in front of high-value customers. You communicate clearly, exercise good judgment, own mistakes when they happen, and help create an environment where others can do the same.

Strong written and visual communication is part of the craft. You can write a paragraph at least as good as this one without the help of an LLM, and you have the editorial judgment to know when a document or slide deck is genuinely ready to present—or when it still needs another pass.

What You’ll Do

This role sits at the center of our customer engagements, bringing together teams of geoscientists, software engineers, and AI/ML engineers to solve complex problems in projects that run for a few months at a time. The work is highly collaborative and varied—from early assessment and scoping through data review and processing, development of code and configurations, machine learning, and ultimately validating and tuning the results.

You will establish yourself as a trusted presence with our customers. Our projects involve high-value relationships around the world, with conversations happening both in person and remotely across time zones. Clear communication matters here, whether that means translating complex technical work for a broader audience, helping a teammate sharpen a presentation, or making sure everyone leaves a conversation with the same understanding of what comes next.

Keeping our projects moving takes equal parts organization, judgment, and curiosity. There are schedules and checklists to manage, decisions to make, changes to navigate, and moments when leadership needs to weigh in. But some of the most important contributions are less procedural: asking the question that helps a team see a problem differently, creating space for a better idea to emerge, helping people through an obstacle, and making sure great work gets recognized when the team succeeds.

We’ve built tools and processes to support this work, but we don’t consider any of them finished. There’s plenty of room to improve what exists, challenge how we do things today, and help build what comes next.

Core Responsibilities

Serve as a primary point of contact across multiple overlapping client projects, owning day-to-day project management and helping ensure successful delivery
Set and manage clear expectations with customers and internal teams throughout each engagement
Build and maintain project plans covering scope, timelines, milestones, risks, decisions, and completion status
Keep important information, decisions, and action items, from falling through the cracks, and make sure commitments are met
Track project health and prioritize using both metrics and your expert judgment
Help improve the playbooks, tools, and templates that allow us to run more client engagements in parallel without sacrificing quality
Identify and manage risks and issues: bring the right people together to resolve them, and escalate thoughtfully when needed
Plan and facilitate effective internal and customer meetings, with clear agendas, decisions, and next steps
Create clear, polished customer-facing materials and help technical team members communicate their work effectively

Qualifications

10+ years of experience in project management, technical program management, implementation, professional services, or a similar role
Experience in a rapidly scaling startup environment is a strong plus
Experience working directly with enterprise customers, ideally delivering software products or services to demanding clients
Demonstrated ability to work closely with scientists and engineers, understanding enough underlying technology to ask good questions and drive great decisions
Experience with software, AI/ML, earth science, physics, or statistical analysis is a plus, but we don’t expect expertise across all of them
Strong judgment around when to introduce structure and process, and when flexibility is the better answer
A solutions-oriented mindset and a track record of navigating ambiguity, changing priorities, and complex projects
Excellent written, verbal, and visual communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across both technical and non-technical audiences
Multilingual communication skills (strong English required, Spanish is a strong plus)
Hybrid work environment at our Redwood City headquarters is preferred; we will consider a remote first role for well qualified candidates residing in the United States, Canada, or Mexico.
All candidates must be legally authorized to live and work, without visa sponsorship, in The United States, Canada, or Mexico.

Compensation & Benefits

The base salary range for this position $185,000-225,000 annually. Actual compensation will depend on experience, qualifications, skills, and other job-related factors. This position is also eligible for equity and Terra AI’s comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, FSA, and a 401(k) with company match.

Terra AI is an equal opportunity employer. We make employment decisions based on qualifications, merit, and business needs, without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, creed, age, disability, medical condition, genetic information, sex, gender, pregnancy or related medical conditions, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, reproductive health decision-making, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

We’re committed to building a workplace where people with different backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives can do their best work. Terra AI also provides reasonable accommodations to qualified applicants and employees with disabilities. If you need an accommodation during the application or interview process, please let us know.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Stanford’s Division of Computational Medicine brings together expertise in biomedical informatics, data science, and medicine to tackle complex questions about human health. We develop computational and statistical methods that help researchers make sense of health data and generate evidence for clinical and translational research.

We are seeking a Research Data Analyst 2 to help reveal how rare diseases emerge in patients’ medical histories. Working with electronic health records from Stanford patients with confirmed diagnoses, you will develop methods to identify patient cohorts and reconstruct diagnostic journeys across 10 rare diseases. Your work will connect information from clinical notes, diagnoses, procedures, medications, and laboratory results to support research on disease recognition and risk modeling.

In this role, you will contribute throughout the research process, from translating clinical questions into computational methods to evaluating results and sharing findings in publications and presentations. You will write Python and SQL code, build tools that bring clinical expertise into method development, and work closely with faculty, clinicians, and technical researchers. This is an opportunity to apply your programming and analytical skills to clinically meaningful questions while deepening your experience in biomedical data science.

Primary Responsibilities

Develop and evaluate methods to identify rare-disease cohorts using structured EHR data and clinical text.
Build reproducible pipelines that organize clinical events into patient diagnostic timelines.
Create annotation and review tools that help clinicians validate extracted information and guide improvements.
Investigate data-quality issues and extraction errors, using clinical feedback to refine computational methods.
Develop performance metrics and automated tests for timeline extraction and downstream disease-risk models.
Translate analyses into clear datasets, figures, reports, presentations, and manuscript contributions.
Document methods, validation results, and limitations so research findings can be understood and reproduced.
Collaborate with clinical and technical colleagues to shape methods, interpret results, and advance the research.

This position offers a hybrid schedule, with onsite work three days per week, subject to operational needs. Please submit a resume and cover letter describing your relevant experience and interest in computational approaches to rare-disease research.

Responsibilities

Core Duties
:

Prioritize and extract data from a variety of sources such as notes, survey results, medical reports, and laboratory data, and maintain its accuracy and completeness.
Determine additional data collection and reporting requirements.
Design and customize reports based upon data in the database. Oversee and monitor regulatory compliance for utilization of the data.
Use system reports and analyses to identify potentially problematic data, make corrections, and eliminate root cause for data problems or justify solutions to be implemented by others.
Create complex charts and databases, perform statistical analyses, and develop graphs and tables for publication and presentation.
Serve as a resource for non-routine inquiries such as requests for statistics or surveys.
Test prototype software and participate in approval and release process for new software.
Provide documentation based on audit and reporting criteria to investigators and research staff.

Minimum Education

Bachelor's degree and three years of relevant experience or combination of education and relevant experience.

Minimum Experience

Experience in a quantitative discipline such as economics, finance, statistics or engineering.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Substantial experience with MS Office and analytical programs.
Excellent writing and analytical skills.
Ability to prioritize workload.

8MSolar is the highest-rated solar energy design and installation firm in North Carolina. We pride ourselves on delivering turnkey, high-quality commercial solar solutions. We offer a dynamic, collaborative, and relaxed workplace culture where employee growth is genuinely supported, safety is prioritized, and hard work is rewarded.

Job Overview

We are seeking a driven, highly organized, and technically skilled Commercial Project Manager to oversee projects from the final point of sale through to final installation and full system activation. This role requires a strong technical aptitude for commercial electrical systems and hands-on solar PV system commissioning. You will be responsible for configuring solar inverter controls, working with common solar PV communications platforms, and diagnosing network interfaces using Modbus TCP, RTU, and SunSpec Modbus standards. You will serve as the primary bridge between our clients and our field execution teams, ensuring multiple parallel commercial projects are delivered safely, on time, and up to our industry-leading quality standards.

Key Responsibilities

Project Execution & Scheduling

Manage workflows on parallel commercial projects, keeping all timelines on track.
Create, update, and transmit detailed project schedules using project management software (Basecamp) and internal accounting sheets.
Identify inventory needs, verify onsite materials, and ensure timely equipment ordering (forklifts, boom lifts, dumpsters, etc.).
Oversee projects seamlessly from contract signing to final closeout.

Electrical Systems & Solar PV Commissioning

Lead the end-to-end commissioning process for commercial solar PV systems, ensuring all equipment operates safely and in accordance with design specifications.
Perform electrical quality assurance (QA/QC), including pre-commissioning checks, string testing (Voc/Isc), insulation resistance testing, and phase rotation verification.
Commission and configure commercial solar inverter controls and Data Acquisition Systems (DAS), ensuring seamless data flow to monitoring platforms.
Diagnose, troubleshoot, and network system communications utilizing Modbus TCP, Modbus RTU, and SunSpec Modbus map protocols to resolve device-level map discrepancies.
Review commercial construction drawings, electrical blueprints, and technical specifications to advise on improvements.
Supervise onsite 8MSolar teams and coordinate mechanical/electrical crews.
Address punch-list items, attend final electrical inspections, and deliver final closeout documentation to clients.

Client & Financial Management

Act as the primary, trusted point of contact for the client throughout the project lifecycle.
Manage the Schedule of Values, billing clients promptly as project milestones are achieved, and tracking payment statuses.

What You Bring (Qualifications)

Education: 4-year technical degree required.
Experience: 3+ years of hands-on experience in the solar industry with a strong focus on field execution and system startup.
Electrical & Commissioning Expertise:
Robust understanding of commercial electrical systems, including three-phase power dynamics, switchgear, transformers, and utility interconnection requirements.
Proven capability insolar PV system commissioning, performance testing, and electrical troubleshooting.

Technical, Networking & Comms Skills

Strong familiarity with common solar PV communication platforms and DAS hardware (e.g., AlsoEnergy/PowerTrack, manufacturer-specific portals like SMA Sunny Portal or SolarEdge, etc.).
Proven capability configuring and diagnosing industrial communication protocols, specifically Modbus TCP/RTU and SunSpec Modbus specifications.
Experience interfacing with site communication hardware including cellular gateways, dataloggers, and environmental sensor arrays (met stations).
Blueprint Literacy: Comfort reading and interpreting electrical blueprints, schematics, three-line diagrams, and network communication diagrams.
Physical & Field Requirements:
Valid NC Driver’s License with a clean driving record.
Ability to operate basic hand/power tools and basic mathematical proficiency.
Ability to lift, carry, push, and pull up to 50 lbs.
Comfortable bending, climbing, squatting, and working onsite in varying weather conditions.
Willingness to work overtime as project schedules demand.

Built for Your Success: Our 6-Week Onboarding Program

We Don’t Expect You To Figure It Out Alone. 8MSolar Invests Heavily In Our Team Members. You Will Go Through a Structured, Paid Onboarding Plan To Set You Up For Long-term Success

Week 6 & Beyond:
Take the reins! Fully manage projects from contract signing to final closeout with the full backing of the 8MSolar team.

Week 1 (Certifications & Tools):
Earn your OSHA-30 and forklift certifications. Get trained on SolarEdge, SMA, UNIRAC, Pegasus, and IronRidge racking guidelines. Master our internal tools (Basecamp, project engineering, and accounting sheets) alongside our leadership team.

Week 2 (Field Foundations):
Head onsite with a Senior Site Supervisor to learn our mechanical/electrical installation nuances and master job site logistics.

Weeks 3–4 (Advanced Electrical & Commissioning):
Focus deeply on electrical installation safety, site evaluations, configuring inverter controls, mapping SunSpec Modbus parameters, and executing full PV system commissioning workflows.

Week 5 (Shadowed Management):
Run a complete mechanical and electrical installation, attend inspections, and conduct client walkthroughs with a Senior Project Engineer right by your side.

jobs.description:
Overview

Join one of the most influential, most quoted, and most trusted think tanks!

The Brookings Institution is a nonprofit public policy organization based in Washington, D.C. Our mission is to equip decision-makers with nonpartisan research and policy strategies to create a more prosperous and secure country and world.

To advance our mission, we are committed to the following four goals:

Develop economic growth strategies for a changing world
Expand economic and social opportunity for all
Revitalize U.S. democratic institutions
Advance peace and security worldwide

At the core of our mission is the quality, independence, and impact of our research. We are dedicated to finding bold, pragmatic solutions for societal challenges through open-minded inquiry, diverse perspectives, and holding ourselves to the highest standards of scholastic rigor.

Beyond the pursuit of excellence and intellectual rigor, Brookings places immense value on creating a supportive and collaborative environment where every individual can do their best work, learn, and grow. Because of this, Brookings has been at the forefront of public policy for more than a century.

The Global Economy and Development program at Brookings aims to shape the policy debate on how to improve global economic cooperation and fight global poverty and sources of social stress.

The Workforce of the Future (WoF) initiative focuses on innovative policy solutions at the intersection of industrial policy, economic development, immigration policy, and the future of work. WoF is seeking a Project Manager and Research Analyst (PMRA) to work closely with the Senior Fellow advance the initiative’s research and policy agenda. This is a dynamic role that combines research, policy analysis, project management, writing, data analytics, and high-profile public engagement.

Note:
Please be advised that Brookings is currently undergoing a multi-year strategic implementation, and as part of this effort, your role, supervisor, and program may change.

Position Location
:
This position is hybrid . Hybrid positions combine regular in-person presence at our Washington, DC office with the option of two days of remote work each week.

Please note:
This position is included in the staff bargaining unit, Brookings United, affiliated with the IFPTE Local 70 union, and is covered under the terms of the collective bargaining agreement.

Responsibilities

Ready to contribute to Brookings success?

The PMRA will bring strong analytical and writing skills, critical thinking, sound judgement, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to manage complex projects and priorities independently. A flexible and entrepreneurial mindset will be essential, always with an eye toward opportunities for innovation and amplifying impact. Responsibilities will include conducting in-depth research and analysis; drafting policy memos, presentations, and other written products; managing complex projects and partnerships; supporting high-profile public engagements and convenings; and serving as a key point of contact for internal and external stakeholders. The PMRA will have the opportunity to engage across a range of policy issues and work closely with researchers, policymakers, and other leaders in the field.

Preference will be given to candidates with expertise in one or more of the following areas: regional economic development; labor economics and workforce policy; AI and its effects on the workforce; and data visualization and interactive tools.

jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.description:
Calling the Brilliant Renegades.

This is your chance to set the vision and lead the teams that will radically transform the future of human health.

The Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) exists to accelerate breakthroughs that are too risky for market capital and too urgent for traditional government. We take on some of the biggest, hardest problems in human health—problems where progress has stalled, risk is high, and the potential impact is enormous.
At ARPA-H, Program Managers (PMs) are the engine of the agency. They identify root-cause bottlenecks, define bold program concepts, recruit exceptional teams, and drive high-risk, high-reward work from idea to real-world impact.
This is not a traditional research role. It is not a grants administrator role.
It is a deeply technical, deeply strategic, deeply mission-driven role—for people who want to make a dent in the universe.
If you have bold ideas to explore, a clear “why now,” and the drive to turn breakthrough science into health outcomes, we encourage you to apply.

What You’ll Do

ARPA-H Program Managers are action-oriented and strong non-traditional thinkers and leaders in breakthrough biotech, health, and R&D. PMs manage ambitious portfolios across academia, industry, and startups and are responsible for compressing decades of progress into years.
As a Program Manager, you will:
Identify problems that matter
— Target root-cause bottlenecks holding back entire fields, not just incremental improvements or single-disease applications.
Find the unlock
— Pinpoint the specific insight, new capability, technology shift, or market change that makes the impossible newly tractable.
Recruit world-class performers
— Assemble top-tier teams across institutions, disciplines, and sectors that would not otherwise work together.
Drive to milestones
— Set aggressive goals, test assumptions quickly, terminate what is not working, and double down on what is.
Shape adoption pathways
— Create the conditions for solutions to be adopted, scaled, and sustained—not just invented.

Program Managers serve an initial three-year term-limited appointment
, which may be extended up to a six-year maximum, to design, launch, and run high-risk, high-reward programs. This limited term is intentional: it brings fresh perspectives, urgency, and sustained momentum.

Who We’re Looking For

We are looking for entrepreneurial, technically exceptional leaders—people who combine deep expertise with intellectual range, fast learning, and the ability to make bold decisions under uncertainty.
You may be the right person if:
You have spent years frustrated that the best science does not become the best medicine fast enough.
You work in systems, not silos.
You have built things before and know the difference between a plan and a theory.
You can hold your own with scientists, clinicians, regulators, investors, operators, and patients—and understand what each group needs to see for a breakthrough to move forward.
You are a rational risk-taker who can navigate failure, learn quickly, and keep moving toward impact.
You want to spend the next chapter of your career working on problems that matter at civilizational scale.

The right candidate will bring:
A bold question to answer
— An ideal for a program with the potential to meaningfully change human health.
An unlock, not just a vision
— A clear explanation of why this can succeed now.
First-principles thinking
— The ability to reason from fundamentals and challenge conventional assumptions.
Ambition and risk appetite
— Comfort pursuing approaches where success is not guaranteed, but impact would be transformative.
Learning velocity
— Demonstrated ability to master new technical areas quickly.
Recruiting power
— A track record of attracting, assembling, and motivating strong teams.
Hands-on experience at the edge
— Practical experience at the intersection of a technical field and biology, medicine, health, or healthcare.
Comfort with term limits
— A desire to build something impactful and hand it off, not build an empire.

ARPA-H describes PMs as “rational risk-takers” with vision and a passion for solving seemingly intractable problems that limit health potential.

This May Not Be the Right Role If

You need a fully defined job description.
You are looking for a prestigious title on the way to something else.
You need to be told what to do.
You are looking for incremental progress.
You are uncomfortable with uncertainty, scrutiny, or the possibility of public failure.

No guaranteed outcomes. No well-trodden paths. No credit if you need it now.
But if it works: the possibility of changing the course of human health.

Required Qualifications

Candidates must meet the following requirements:
U.S. citizenship required.
ARPA-H employment eligibility is limited to U.S. citizens
Technical degree required.
Ph.D., M.D., or Master’s degree in a scientific or engineering field.
Post-education experience.
At least one professional role after completing the qualifying degree.
Bio/health intersection.
Demonstrated experience applying technical expertise in a biological, medical, health, or healthcare context.
Geographic flexibility.
Willingness to be in Washington, D.C. at least once per month, especially during the first year.
Public trust-level clearance.
Selected candidates are required to undergo a background investigation
Ethics and financial review.
Must complete required ethics and financial disclosure reviews as part of the federal onboarding process.
Conflict of interest assessment.
Must undergo review to identify and mitigate any real or perceived conflicts related to official duties and outside activities.

Compensation

Competitive with academia and the private sector.

Hiring Authority: At ARPA-H, our customer is the American public, and we seek to build a mission-driven workforce as representative as our customer base. We are building a culture that creates a space for visionary innovators in science, health, and in building a best-in-class ARPA organization. For this position, ARPA-H has been authorized a special hiring authority that that allows for more flexibility around hiring timelines and pay-setting.

Equal Employment Opportunity: Selection for this position will be based solely on merit with no discrimination for reasons such as race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, national origin, political affiliation, marital status, disability, age, or membership/non-membership in an employee organization. ARPA-H encourages the application and nomination of qualified women, minorities, and individuals with disabilities.

Reasonable Accommodation: ARPA-H provide a reasonable accommodation to applicants with disabilities. If you require reasonable accommodation during any part of the application and hiring process, please notify us. The decision on granting reasonable accommodation will be made on a case-bycase basis.

Standards of Conduct/Financial Disclosure: ARPA-H inspires public confidence in our work by maintaining high ethical principles. ARPA-H employees are subject to Federal government-wide regulations and statutes as well as agency-specific regulations described on the NIH Ethics website. We encourage you to review this information. The position requires the incumbent to complete a public financial disclosure report prior to the effective date of the appointment.

Foreign Education: Applicants who have completed part or all of their education outside of the U.S. must have their foreign education evaluated by an accredited organization to ensure that the foreign education is equivalent to education received in accredited educational institutions in the U.S. We will only accept the completed foreign education evaluation. For more information on foreign education verification, visit https://www.naces.org. Verification must be received prior to the effective date of the appointment.
